2) Core rules and shared function detection (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, Core Functionality): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts * export const DEFAULT_SCOPE = ["FunctionDeclaration", "FunctionExpression", "MethodDefinition", "TSMethodSignature", "TSDeclareFunction"]; * Arrow functions are not in DEFAULT_SCOPE, matching the story’s "Arrow functions are excluded by default". - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts re-exports DEFAULT_SCOPE and defines: * function shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority = "all") { ... } that checks node.type in scope and applies exportPriority. - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts * imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from "./helpers/require-story-helpers". * meta.schema: scope is array of enum DEFAULT_SCOPE, exportPriority is enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. * create(context) computes scope = opts.scope || DEFAULT_SCOPE and exportPriority = opts.exportPriority || "all" and passes a shouldProcessNode wrapper into buildVisitors(). - src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts * Options type includes scope?: (typeof DEFAULT_SCOPE)[number][], exportPriority?: (typeof EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES)[number]. * meta.schema mirrors require-story-annotation: scope array of DEFAULT_SCOPE enums; exportPriority enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. * create(context) computes scope defaulting to DEFAULT_SCOPE and exportPriority defaulting to "all", then uses shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) in a local shouldCheck. * Registers visitors for: FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (skipping MethodDefinition parent), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature — exactly the five node types in DEFAULT_SCOPE. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts (used only by require-story-annotation): * buildFunctionDeclarationVisitor → FunctionDeclaration handler, uses options.shouldProcessNode and helperReportMissing. * buildFunctionExpressionVisitor → FunctionExpression handler, uses options.shouldProcessNode and skips MethodDefinition parents. * buildMethodDefinitionVisitor → MethodDefinition handler, uses options.shouldProcessNode and helperReportMethod. * buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor → TSDeclareFunction handler. * buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor → TSMethodSignature handler. * buildArrowFunctionVisitor → ArrowFunctionExpression handler, but DEFAULT_SCOPE does not include ArrowFunctionExpression and the rule schema restricts scope to DEFAULT_SCOPE enums, so options.shouldProcessNode always returns false for arrows under valid configuration. This satisfies "Arrow functions are excluded by default" while allowing future extension. - Conclusion: Both rules enforce on the same set of function-like constructs and exclude arrow functions by default, satisfying REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION and the Core Functionality criterion.
3) JSDoc parsing and common strategy (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING, Error Handling): - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts * jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node) uses sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node) and checks jsdoc.value.includes("@story"). * commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node) uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) and scans for "@story". * leadingCommentsHasStory(node) scans node.leadingComments for "@story". * hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node) composes jsdocHasStory, commentsBeforeHasStory, leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory inside a try/catch — it returns false on errors instead of throwing, matching the Error Handling acceptance criterion. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-io.ts * LOOKBACK_LINES and FALLBACK_WINDOW constants centralize heuristic window sizes. * linesBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node, lookback=LOOKBACK_LINES) scans a limited line window before the node for "@story" or "@supports" with guards against missing lines/loc. * parentChainHasStory(sourceCode, node) walks parents and inspects getCommentsBefore and leadingComments for "@story" or "@supports". * fallbackTextBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node) slices sourceCode.getText() in a bounded window defined by FALLBACK_WINDOW, checking for "@story" or "@supports" and swallowing IO/slicing errors. - src/utils/annotation-checker.ts * getJsdocComment, getLeadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments abstract JSDoc and comment retrieval. * checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options) uses those helpers and calls hasReqAnnotation(...) from src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts; on false it reports missing @req. - src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts * hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context, node) uses linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq (which mirror the story IO logic) inside try/catch and falls back to simple jsdoc.value/includes and commentContainsReq. * commentContainsReq treats both "@req" and "@supports" as evidence of requirement coverage. - This demonstrates a shared, robust JSDoc/comment parsing strategy for both @story and @req, with multiple heuristics and guarded error handling.

Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') referencing the appropriate requirement from the story file." * create(context) registers the five function-like visitors; each uses checkReqAnnotation(context, node, { enableFix: false }) so the rule enforces presence while delegating detection and error reporting to shared helpers. * tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts invalid cases cover: - Missing @req on FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (named and anonymous/IIFE), MethodDefinition in classes and object literals, TS FunctionExpressions, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - Each asserts messageId "missingReq" with data { name: ..., functionName: ... }, verifying user-friendly and precise error messages at function identifiers. - Together, these show that when both rules are enabled, functions are expected to carry both @story and @req annotations, satisfying REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED and the story's core value.

traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and detailed requirements in docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are implemented and verified. The two core ESLint rules, require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation, share a common detection scope (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature), explicitly exclude arrow functions by default, use a shared and robust JSDoc/comment parsing strategy, and support consistent scope and exportPriority configuration. Errors are reported at function names with clear, actionable messages and suggestions. TypeScript-specific constructs TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature are handled symmetrically across both rules and covered by dedicated tests. Both rules have comprehensive documentation that matches the implemented behavior and are integrated into the plugin’s recommended and strict configs. All associated RuleTester suites and helper tests referenced by this story pass in the project’s Jest test run, so the story is fully satisfied.
